gates: Windows 10/11 Pro or Education, 64-bit, with at least 16 GB RAM and 80 GB free disk — Server runs inside a virtual machine, not on bare metal.
A working hypervisor: Hyper-V (see IL27-INST-03) or VirtualBox (see IL27-INST-16). Install one first.

Download the Windows Server 2025 evaluation ISO from the official Microsoft Evaluation Center (search 'Windows Server 2025 evaluation'). Choose ISO, English, 64-bit. The evaluation is free and re-armable.

Create a new Generation 2 VM (Hyper-V) or EFI-enabled VM (VirtualBox): 4 vCPU, 8 GB RAM (8192 MB), 100 GB dynamically expanding VHD/VDI, attach the ISO as the DVD drive, disable Secure Boot temporarily if the VM refuses to boot from ISO.
Boot the VM, install Server with Desktop Experience (NOT Server Core for this lab), set a strong local Administrator password, and complete the out-of-box setup.
After first logon, in the VM open Settings > Network and assign a static IP on your lab subnet (e.g. 192.168.56.10, mask 255.255.255.0). You will promote this box to a domain controller later.

checkpoints.expected: Shows 5.1.x — stock Windows PowerShell on the new Server build
WindowsProductName: Microsoft Windows Server 2025 Standard Evaluation (Desktop Experience)
Your chosen static lab IP, e.g. 192.168.56.10
True — the VM reaches the internet through the host NAT

troubleshoot.issue: VM boots to a black screen / 'no bootable device'
troubleshoot.fix: Re-attach the ISO to the virtual DVD drive and move DVD to the top of the boot order; on Gen 2 Hyper-V VMs confirm Secure Boot is off during install.

troubleshoot.issue: Setup says the product key is invalid
troubleshoot.fix: Click 'I don't have a product key' — the evaluation edition installs without one and activates its 180-day timer automatically.

troubleshoot.issue: VM is unusably slow
troubleshoot.fix: Raise RAM to 8 GB minimum and give it 4 vCPUs; confirm virtualization (Intel VT-x/AMD-V) is enabled in the host BIOS/UEFI.

costNote: Free: the evaluation ISO is a 180-day trial from the Microsoft Evaluation Center, re-armable a few times with slmgr.vbs /rearm. No purchase needed for the full IL-27 homelab.

gates: Windows 11 Pro (or Windows 10 1809+) on your admin workstation — RSAT installs as optional Features on Demand, not a separate download.

Open Settings > Apps > Optional features > View features, search for 'RSAT', and install at minimum: 'RSAT: Active Directory Domain Services and Lightweight Directory Services Tools' and 'RSAT: DHCP Server Tools' and 'RSAT: DNS Server Tools'.

Alternative (admin PowerShell, same result): Get-WindowsCapability -Online | Where-Object Name -like 'Rsat.ActiveDirectory*' | Add-WindowsCapability -Online, then repeat for Rsat.DHCP* and Rsat.DNS*. Wait for State: Installed.
Close and reopen your admin tools: press Win+R, type dsa.msc — the Active Directory Users and Computers console should open. If it errors, the AD DS tools capability is not installed yet.
Join your workstation to the lab domain later (IL27 tool lab chain) — RSAT works against the domain once DNS points at your domain controller.

checkpoints.expected: At least one Rsat.ActiveDirectory* capability listed with State Installed
ActiveDirectory module listed (version 1.0.0.0)
Count well above 100 — the full AD cmdlet set is present

troubleshoot.issue: Add-WindowsCapability fails with 0x800f0954 or download errors
troubleshoot.fix: The machine must reach Windows Update. If WSUS is in play, temporarily allow the Features-on-Demand download: set the group policy 'Specify settings for optional component installation' or run the command with -Source pointing at install media.

troubleshoot.issue: dsa.msc opens but shows no domain / access denied
troubleshoot.fix: Your workstation is not domain-joined or DNS does not point at the DC. Set the workstation DNS to the DC's IP first, then join the domain.

costNote: Free: RSAT is built into Windows 10/11 Pro as optional features; no license beyond the OS.

gates: Windows 10/11 Pro, Education, or Enterprise 64-bit — Hyper-V is NOT available on Home. CPU must support SLAT (second-level address translation); virtually all CPUs from the last decade do.
Enable virtualization in firmware: reboot into BIOS/UEFI, turn on Intel VT-x / AMD-V (often under Advanced > CPU Configuration). Save and boot back to Windows.
Open an elevated PowerShell and run: Enable-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName Microsoft-Hyper-V -All. Reboot when prompted — the reboot is mandatory.

After reboot, open Hyper-V Manager (virtmgmt.msc). In the Actions pane open Virtual Switch Manager and create an External virtual switch bound to your physical NIC (for internet access) plus an Internal switch named 'Lab-Internal' for the isolated lab network.
Create a test VM (Generation 2, 2 GB RAM, 30 GB disk), attach any ISO, and boot it to prove the hypervisor works before you build the real lab VMs.

checkpoints.expected: State: Enabled
Your External switch (SwitchType External) and Lab-Internal (SwitchType Internal) listed
Your test VM listed (State Off or Running)
All lines report 'Yes'

troubleshoot.issue: Enable-WindowsOptionalFeature says Hyper-V cannot be installed
troubleshoot.fix: You are on Windows Home, or VT-x/AMD-V is off in firmware, or Hyper-V's hypervisor conflicts with another hypervisor — disable Memory Integrity / VirtualBox's hypervisor use, enable VT-x, retry.

troubleshoot.issue: VM has no network
troubleshoot.fix: Check the VM is attached to the External switch for internet (or Lab-Internal for isolated). External switches break if the host NIC driver was replaced — recreate the switch.

troubleshoot.issue: VirtualBox VMs fail after enabling Hyper-V
troubleshoot.fix: VirtualBox 6.1+ can run under Hyper-V but slowly; either use Hyper-V for everything or disable Hyper-V and use VirtualBox exclusively — pick one hypervisor per host.

costNote: Free: Hyper-V is included with Windows Pro/Education/Enterprise at no extra cost.

gates: Windows: download the MSI from the PowerShell GitHub releases page (search 'PowerShell releases', take the latest 7.x LTS win-x64 MSI). Run it, check 'Add to PATH' and 'Register Windows Event Logging Manifest' during setup.

Linux (Ubuntu/Debian): the Microsoft package repo route — download the .deb from the same releases page and install with: sudo dpkg -i powershell_*.deb && sudo apt-get install -f. Or register the Microsoft repo and apt install powershell.
Launch the new shell: type pwsh in Windows Terminal / Start menu, or run pwsh on Linux. Confirm the banner says PowerShell 7.x, not 5.1.

Install the two modules every IL-27 script lab uses: Install-Module -Name PSScriptAnalyzer -Force and, on Windows, confirm the ActiveDirectory module auto-loads when RSAT is present (Import-Module ActiveDirectory).
Set your execution policy for scripting: Set-ExecutionPolicy RemoteSigned -Scope CurrentUser (Windows). On Linux no policy applies; scripts run once chmod +x is set.

checkpoints.expected: Major 7 (e.g. 7.4.x or 7.5.x) — NOT 5.1
A version number — the analyzer module is installed
(Windows) RemoteSigned

troubleshoot.issue: 'pwsh' is not recognized after install
troubleshoot.fix: Close and reopen the terminal so PATH refreshes; the MSI's 'Add to PATH' box must be checked — repair the install if it was missed.

troubleshoot.issue: Install-Module fails: 'Unable to resolve package source'
troubleshoot.fix: The PSGallery is unreachable — check proxy/internet, then run Register-PSRepository -Default and retry.

troubleshoot.issue: Linux: pwsh starts but ActiveDirectory cmdlets are missing
troubleshoot.fix: Expected — the AD module is Windows-only. Do AD work from the Windows admin workstation or via PowerShell remoting to the DC.

costNote: Free and open source (MIT license) on every platform.

tool: Active Directory Domain Services lab (first domain controller)
gates: Complete IL27-INST-01: a Windows Server 2025 VM with a static IP, joined to no domain yet, logged on as local Administrator.
Install the AD DS role (elevated PowerShell on the Server): Install-WindowsFeature AD-Domain-Services -IncludeManagementTools. Wait for Success = True.

Promote to a domain controller: Import-Module ADDSDeployment, then Install-ADDSForest -DomainName 'lab.local' -DomainNetbiosName 'LAB' -InstallDns:$true -SafeModeAdministratorPassword (Read-Host -AsSecureString 'DSRM password') -Force. The server reboots automatically.
After reboot, log on as LAB\Administrator. Verify DNS: the server should have the DNS Server role installed (promoted with -InstallDns) and its own NIC DNS should point at 127.0.0.1.

Create your lab OU structure with ADUC or PowerShell: OU=Workstations, OU=Servers, OU=Users, OU=Groups, OU=ServiceAccounts under the domain root. Everything later in the course lives inside these OUs.
Raise the bar: set the Default Domain Password Policy (fine-grained comes later) — minimum length 12, complexity on — via Group Policy Management on the DC.

checkpoints.expected: DNSRoot: lab.local, NetBIOSName: LAB, a current DomainMode
Your server listed, IsGlobalCatalog: True
Workstations, Servers, Users, Groups, ServiceAccounts listed
No output — quiet means every test passed

troubleshoot.issue: Install-ADDSForest fails: 'verification of prerequisites failed' on DNS
troubleshoot.fix: Give the server a static IP and set its DNS to itself (127.0.0.1) BEFORE promoting; promotion with DHCP-assigned DNS fails the checks.

troubleshoot.issue: dcdiag reports DNS failures after promotion
troubleshoot.fix: Wait 10 minutes for initial replication/DNS registration, then run ipconfig /registerdns and nltest /dsregdns, and re-run dcdiag.

troubleshoot.issue: Forgot the DSRM password
troubleshoot.fix: Reset it from an elevated prompt on the DC: ntdsutil 'set dsrm password' 'reset password on server <DCname>' q q — you need Domain Admin rights.

costNote: Free inside the homelab: uses the Server 2025 evaluation from IL27-INST-01. Never promote a trial DC in production.

gates: Windows: download the 64-bit installer from the official Wireshark site (search 'Wireshark download'), run it, accept the Npcap driver install when offered — without Npcap you cannot capture.

Linux (Ubuntu): sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y wireshark. During install, answer Yes to 'should non-superusers be able to capture packets', then add yourself to the group: sudo usermod -aG wireshark $USER and log out/in.
Launch Wireshark, double-click your active interface (Ethernet or Wi-Fi) to start a capture. You should immediately see packets scrolling.

Learn the two filters you will use all course: type dns in the display filter bar to see only DNS, then icmp. Capture while you run ping and nslookup in another window to watch the traffic you generate.
Practice a capture filter at start time: on the welcome screen, set the capture filter to 'port 53' on the interface before starting — this keeps captures small and focused on DNS.

checkpoints.expected: Wireshark 4.x.x with Npcap/libpcap listed

checkpoints.command: In Wireshark: Statistics > Protocol Hierarchy after a 30-second capture
checkpoints.expected: A protocol breakdown (Ethernet/IP/TCP/DNS/...) — capture is working
DNS packets printed for 5 seconds, then clean exit

troubleshoot.issue: No interfaces listed / 'no interfaces found'
troubleshoot.fix: Windows: reinstall and make sure the Npcap box was checked. Linux: you are not in the wireshark group — run the usermod command and fully log out and back in.

troubleshoot.issue: Capture starts but shows zero packets
troubleshoot.fix: Wrong interface selected (e.g. a disconnected virtual adapter) — stop, pick the interface with the live IP, and check the capture filter syntax.

troubleshoot.issue: Promiscuous mode shows nothing extra on Wi-Fi
troubleshoot.fix: Normal: most Wi-Fi drivers do not deliver other clients' traffic. Capture your own traffic; use the lab's wired/virtual interfaces for full visibility.

gates: Download the pfSense CE (or OPNsense) amd64 ISO from the official project site. Either satisfies this lab — the concepts transfer; pfSense is used in the examples.
Create a VM with TWO virtual NICs: NIC 1 attached to your External switch (WAN side), NIC 2 attached to 'Lab-Internal' (LAN side). 2 vCPU, 2 GB RAM, 16 GB disk is plenty.
Boot the ISO and install: accept defaults, choose Auto (ZFS) or Auto (UFS) partitioning, install to the virtual disk, remove the ISO and reboot.
At the console menu, assign interfaces: WAN = the NIC on the External switch (vtnet0/em0), LAN = the NIC on Lab-Internal. Set the LAN IP to 192.168.10.1/24 when prompted.

From your host browser, open https://192.168.10.1 (reach it via a VM on Lab-Internal, or add a temporary host route). Log in with admin/pfsense and run the Setup Wizard: set hostname, DNS, timezone, change the admin password immediately.
Enable DHCP on LAN (Services > DHCP Server) for 192.168.10.100-200 so lab VMs get addresses automatically. This firewall becomes the lab's network core for every later module.

checkpoints.expected: Replies — the firewall LAN interface is up

checkpoints.command: From a lab VM: nslookup google.com 192.168.10.1  (or via browser: Diagnostics > DNS Lookup)
checkpoints.expected: A resolved address — the firewall's DNS forwarder works

checkpoints.command: In the web UI: Status > Dashboard
checkpoints.expected: Dashboard loads showing WAN IP (from your real network) and LAN 192.168.10.1

troubleshoot.issue: Cannot reach https://192.168.10.1
troubleshoot.fix: Your test VM must sit on the Lab-Internal switch with an IP in 192.168.10.0/24 — a VM on the External switch cannot route to it. Check which vSwitch each VM uses.

troubleshoot.issue: WAN shows 0.0.0.0 / no internet behind the firewall
troubleshoot.fix: WAN NIC is on the wrong vSwitch or the upstream network needs DHCP — at the console, re-run interface assignment (option 1) and confirm WAN gets a DHCP address.

troubleshoot.issue: Web UI certificate warning
troubleshoot.fix: Expected: pfSense uses a self-signed cert. Click through the warning (Advanced > Proceed) — or install the firewall CA later for clean HTTPS.

costNote: Free and open source (pfSense CE / OPNsense). Runs fine on the homelab host.

gates: Download the Ubuntu Server 24.04 LTS ISO from ubuntu.com/download/server (take the LTS, not the interim release).
Create a VM: 2 vCPU, 4 GB RAM, 40 GB disk, NIC on your lab network (Lab-Internal behind pfSense, or bridged — pick Lab-Internal to match the course).
Install: choose English, set hostname 'lab-linux01', create your user (e.g. 'ops'), install the OpenSSH server when offered, and let the installer use the whole disk with LVM.

On first boot, update everything: sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade -y. Then lock SSH down: edit /etc/ssh/sshd_config to set PasswordAuthentication no AFTER you have copied your public key in (ssh-copy-id ops@<ip>), then sudo systemctl restart ssh.

Give the server a static IP via netplan: edit /etc/netplan/50-cloud-init.yaml with addresses: [192.168.10.20/24], gateway4 via 192.168.10.1, nameservers to your DC (192.168.56.10) or pfSense (192.168.10.1). Apply with sudo netplan apply.
Install the lab toolkit: sudo apt install -y htop curl wget git unzip net-tools dnsutils.

checkpoints.expected: Ubuntu 24.04.x LTS
active
Your static 192.168.10.20/24 on the primary NIC
key-auth-ok — key-based SSH works, passwords rejected

troubleshoot.issue: Locked out of SSH after disabling passwords
troubleshoot.fix: Use the hypervisor console to log in locally, re-enable PasswordAuthentication yes, restart ssh, copy your key properly, then disable passwords again.

troubleshoot.issue: netplan apply breaks networking
troubleshoot.fix: YAML is whitespace-sensitive — two-space indents, no tabs. Restore from /etc/netplan backup or console in and fix indentation.

troubleshoot.issue: apt update fails with DNS errors
troubleshoot.fix: The VM has no DNS: check /etc/netplan nameservers point at 192.168.10.1 or your DC, and that the pfSense LAN allows outbound DNS.

gates: Windows: download Docker Desktop from docker.com/products/docker-desktop, run the installer, keep 'Use WSL 2 instead of Hyper-V' checked (WSL 2 backend is the modern default). Reboot if asked.

Linux: Docker Desktop for Linux exists, but the course uses Docker Engine on the Ubuntu VM instead (IL27-INST-08): curl -fsSL https://get.docker.com | sh, then sudo usermod -aG docker $USER and log out/in.
Start Docker Desktop, wait for the whale icon to stop animating (engine running), then open a terminal and run: docker run hello-world.
Pull the images the course reuses: docker pull nginx:alpine and docker pull zabbix/zabbix-server-mysql:alpine-latest (for the monitoring module's container option).
Learn the lifecycle trio you will repeat all course: docker ps (what's running), docker logs <name> (why it failed), docker rm -f <name> (clean up).

checkpoints.expected: Docker version 2x.x and Compose v2.x reported
'Hello from Docker!' — engine pulls and runs containers
nginx:alpine and the zabbix image listed locally

troubleshoot.issue: Docker Desktop: 'WSL 2 installation is incomplete'
troubleshoot.fix: Install the WSL 2 kernel update package from Microsoft (the error dialog links it), or run wsl --install in an elevated prompt, then restart Docker Desktop.

troubleshoot.issue: 'permission denied' on docker commands (Linux)
troubleshoot.fix: Your user is not in the docker group yet — run the usermod command and fully log out and back in; do not chmod the socket.

troubleshoot.issue: Containers cannot reach the internet
troubleshoot.fix: Docker's embedded DNS/iptables needs a working host network; restart Docker Desktop, and on corporate VPNs add the VPN DNS to Docker Desktop > Settings > Docker Engine 'dns' array.

costNote: Free for personal/educational use (Docker Personal subscription).

gates: Use your Ubuntu Server VM (IL27-INST-08). Install Zabbix 7.x from the official Zabbix repository: download the zabbix-release .deb for Ubuntu 24.04 from zabbix.com/download, dpkg -i it, apt update.

Install the server stack: sudo apt install -y zabbix-server-mysql zabbix-frontend-php zabbix-apache-conf zabbix-sql-scripts zabbix-agent2. Also install MySQL/MariaDB if not present: sudo apt install -y mariadb-server.

Create the database: sudo mysql -e "CREATE DATABASE zabbix CHARACTER SET utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_bin; CREATE USER 'zabbix'@'localhost' IDENTIFIED BY 'Str0ngLabPass!'; GRANT ALL ON zabbix.* TO 'zabbix'@'localhost'; SET GLOBAL log_bin_trust_function_creators=1;" then import the schema: zcat /usr/share/zabbix-sql-scripts/mysql/server.sql.gz | mysql --default-character-set=utf8mb4 -u zabbix -p zabbix, then set log_bin_trust_function_creators back to 0.

Point the server at the DB: edit /etc/zabbix/zabbix_server.conf, set DBPassword=Str0ngLabPass!, then systemctl restart zabbix-server zabbix-agent2 apache2 and enable them: systemctl enable zabbix-server zabbix-agent2 apache2.

Open http://<ubuntu-ip>/zabbix, log in as Admin/zabbix, change the password immediately, and run through the frontend wizard. Add your Windows Server VM as a host with the Zabbix agent template (install zabbix-agent2 on Windows via the MSI from zabbix.com/download).

checkpoints.command: systemctl is-active zabbix-server zabbix-agent2 apache2 mariadb
checkpoints.expected: active on all four lines
Listeners on 10051 (server), 10050 (agent), 80 (frontend)

checkpoints.command: In the Zabbix UI: Monitoring > Hosts
checkpoints.expected: 'Zabbix server' shows green ZBIX icon; your Windows host appears once the agent is installed

troubleshoot.issue: Frontend shows 'Unable to connect to database'
troubleshoot.fix: DBPassword in zabbix_server.conf does not match the MariaDB user — re-check the password and that the zabbix database import completed without errors.
Stale lock from a crashed start: sudo rm -f /run/zabbix/zabbix_server.pid and restart the service.

troubleshoot.issue: Windows host stays grey/unreachable in Zabbix
troubleshoot.fix: The Windows agent's Server= must list the Zabbix server IP, and TCP 10050 must be open on the Windows firewall — the agent MSI can add the rule if you tick the box.

costNote: Free and open source (GPL). Self-hosted — no cloud account needed.

gates: On the Ubuntu VM, the fastest course path is Docker Compose. Create ~/monitoring/docker-compose.yml with two services: prom/prometheus:latest (port 9090) and grafana/grafana-oss:latest (port 3000), each with a named volume.
Add a prometheus.yml next to it with a global scrape_interval of 15s and a job 'prometheus' targeting localhost:9090. Start it: docker compose up -d.
Open http://<ubuntu-ip>:9090 — the Prometheus expression browser. Run the query up to prove self-scraping works (expect 1).
Open http://<ubuntu-ip>:3000, log in as admin/admin, change the password, then add Prometheus as a data source (URL http://prometheus:9090 — container DNS name, not localhost).

Add a Linux target: install node_exporter on the Ubuntu host (sudo apt install -y prometheus-node-exporter), add a 'node' job scraping <ubuntu-ip>:9100, and import Grafana dashboard ID 1860 (Node Exporter Full) to see host metrics.

checkpoints.expected: prometheus and grafana containers Up
JSON with status success and a result for the up metric
Time series returned once the node_exporter job is added

troubleshoot.issue: Grafana data source test fails
troubleshoot.fix: From inside the grafana container, 'localhost:9090' is Grafana itself — use the Compose service name http://prometheus:9090.

troubleshoot.issue: Dashboard 1860 shows 'No data'
troubleshoot.fix: The node_exporter job is missing or the target is down: check Prometheus Status > Targets and confirm <ip>:9100 is UP.

troubleshoot.issue: Ports 9090/3000 unreachable from the host
troubleshoot.fix: The compose ports mapping must be '9090:9090' style; on the VM check ss -tlnp and the host firewall/NSG equivalent.

tool: Windows Server Backup + Veeam Agent Free
gates: Windows Server Backup (WSB): on the Server 2025 VM, run Install-WindowsFeature Windows-Server-Backup -IncludeManagementTools. Attach a dedicated virtual disk (at least 60 GB) to the VM to serve as the backup target — never back up to the same disk you are protecting.
Open wbadmin.msc (Windows Server Backup console). Run a one-time backup: Backup Once > Full server > save to your dedicated backup disk. Time it — this is your baseline full-backup duration.

Schedule it: in the console choose Backup Schedule > Full server > daily at 02:00, target the dedicated disk. Confirm with: wbadmin get versions (after the first scheduled run) or check Task Scheduler > Microsoft > Windows > Backup.

Veeam Agent for Windows (Free): download from veeam.com (free edition), install on your admin workstation, create a backup job: Entire computer > target an external USB or network share, schedule weekly full + daily incremental, enable application-aware processing.

Test the only thing that matters — a restore: on the Server, run wbadmin start recovery -version:<id from get versions> -itemType:File -items:C:\RestoreTest -recoveryTarget:C:\RestoreTestOut after placing a canary file, and confirm the canary comes back.

checkpoints.expected: Installed: True
At least one backup version listed with timestamp
No backup in progress / last backup succeeded (or idle)
Backup job configured, last run Success

troubleshoot.issue: wbadmin fails: 'not enough disk space on target'
troubleshoot.fix: The target disk must exceed the used space of all backed-up volumes; attach a bigger dedicated VHD and re-target the schedule.

troubleshoot.issue: Scheduled backup never runs
troubleshoot.fix: The Task Scheduler task runs as SYSTEM — confirm the target disk is online at 02:00 (no sleep on the VM host) and check Microsoft-Windows-Backup event log for the failure code.

troubleshoot.issue: Veeam job fails writing to a network share
troubleshoot.fix: The share credentials in the job must have write rights; test with net use \\<share> <user> first, and confirm SMB is allowed through the firewall.

costNote: Windows Server Backup is included with Server. Veeam Agent Free edition is free for personal/lab use.

gates: On your admin workstation or a Server VM, install the Windows ADK (Assessment and Deployment Kit) for Windows 11 / Server 2025 from the Microsoft site: take the ADK Setup plus the WinPE add-on — MDT cannot build boot images without WinPE.
Install MDT itself (MicrosoftDeploymentToolkit_x64.msi from the Microsoft Download Center). Open the Deployment Workbench — you should see 'Deployment Shares' in the tree.
Create a deployment share: right-click Deployment Shares > New Deployment Share, path D:\DeploymentShare$, share name DeploymentShare$. Accept the defaults through the wizard.
Import an OS: right-click Operating Systems > Import Operating System > Full set of source files, point at a mounted Windows 11 ISO's Sources folder. This stages install.wim for deployment.

Update the deployment share (right-click > Update Deployment Share) to generate LiteTouchPE_x64.iso/.wim — this is the boot image you would PXE-boot or USB-boot target machines with. You do not need to deploy to real hardware for this lab; understanding the share structure IS the deliverable.
Open D:\DeploymentShare$\Control\CustomSettings.ini and add a [Default] section with SkipBDDWelcome=YES and TimeZoneName=Eastern Standard Time — your first taste of MDT automation rules.

checkpoints.expected: MDT installed; Deployment Workbench opens
True — boot media generated
Your imported Windows 11 OS folder listed

troubleshoot.issue: 'Update Deployment Share' fails generating WinPE
troubleshoot.fix: The WinPE add-on for the matching ADK version is missing — install the adkwinpesetup.exe for the same ADK release and retry.

troubleshoot.issue: Import OS fails with DISM errors
troubleshoot.fix: Run the Workbench elevated; confirm the ISO's install.wim/install.esd is readable (copy the Sources folder locally first).

troubleshoot.issue: DeploymentShare$ not accessible over the network
troubleshoot.fix: The wizard sets share permissions — verify with Get-SmbShare DeploymentShare$ and that the lab firewall allows SMB from target machines.

costNote: Free: MDT and the Windows ADK are free downloads. (Production use needs proper Windows licensing for deployed OSes.)

tool: Windows Terminal + VS Code (admin workstation setup)
gates: Install Windows Terminal from the Microsoft Store (search 'Windows Terminal') — or winget install Microsoft.WindowsTerminal. Pin it to the taskbar; this is your daily driver from now on.
Open Terminal settings (Ctrl+,) and set PowerShell 7 (pwsh) as the default profile so every new tab opens in 7.x, not 5.1.

Install VS Code from code.visualstudio.com (User Installer, 64-bit). On first launch install the PowerShell extension (ms-vscode.powershell) — it gives you IntelliSense, a debugger, and PSScriptAnalyzer squiggles.
In VS Code, open the Command Palette (Ctrl+Shift+P) > 'PowerShell: Open Examples Folder' to see sample scripts, then set your integrated terminal default to pwsh as well.

Create your profile: in pwsh run notepad $PROFILE, add Set-PSReadLineOption -PredictionSource HistoryAndPlugin and a prompt function showing the computer name — you will live in this shell for the automation module.

checkpoints.expected: A Windows Terminal version number
VS Code version, commit hash, architecture lines
ms-vscode.powershell listed
Major 7 — the default profile is pwsh

troubleshoot.issue: New Terminal tabs still open PowerShell 5.1
troubleshoot.fix: Settings > Startup > Default profile — pick 'PowerShell' (the 7.x one, with the blue icon), not 'Windows PowerShell'.

troubleshoot.issue: VS Code PowerShell extension shows 'no PowerShell found'
troubleshoot.fix: Point the extension at pwsh: settings 'powershell.powerShellExePath' = the pwsh.exe path from (Get-Command pwsh).Source.

troubleshoot.issue: $PROFILE edits do not load
troubleshoot.fix: You edited the profile for the wrong host — $PROFILE differs between pwsh and Windows PowerShell. Edit the path that $PROFILE prints inside pwsh itself.

costNote: Free: both are free and open source.

gates: Windows 10/11 already ships the OpenSSH client: in an elevated PowerShell run Get-WindowsCapability -Online | Where-Object Name -like 'OpenSSH.Client*' — State should be Installed; if not, Add-WindowsCapability -Online -Name OpenSSH.Client~~~~0.0.1.0.
Test it against your Ubuntu VM: ssh ops@192.168.10.20. Accept the host key on first connect and confirm key-based login works (set up in IL27-INST-08).

Install PuTTY (putty.org or winget install PuTTY.PuTTY) for the GUI workflow: create a saved session 'lab-linux01' with the Ubuntu IP, and under Connection > SSH > Auth load your private key (.ppk via PuTTYgen, or native OpenSSH key in newer PuTTY).

Generate a dedicated lab keypair if you have not: ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C 'il27-lab' -f $HOME\.ssh\il27_lab (no passphrase for the lab, or use ssh-agent). Copy the public key to the Ubuntu VM with ssh-copy-id or manual append to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys.

Bonus: enable the OpenSSH SERVER on your admin workstation (Add-WindowsCapability OpenSSH.Server) so you can practice remoting INTO Windows later: Start-Service sshd; Set-Service sshd -StartupType Automatic.

checkpoints.expected: OpenSSH version string (client present)
lab-linux01 — non-interactive key auth succeeds

checkpoints.command: Get-Service sshd | Select-Object Status  (if server enabled)
checkpoints.expected: Status: Running

troubleshoot.issue: ssh asks for a password despite your key
troubleshoot.fix: Server-side permissions: ~/.ssh must be 700 and authorized_keys 600, owned by you. On Windows-hosted sshd, the key goes in %USERPROFILE%\.ssh\authorized_keys with strict ACLs — use the ssh-agent instead if ACLs fight you.

troubleshoot.issue: 'Connection timed out' to the Ubuntu VM
troubleshoot.fix: Wrong vSwitch/IP or the VM firewall: confirm ping works first, then sudo ufw allow OpenSSH on the VM if UFW is active.

troubleshoot.issue: PuTTY 'Server refused our key'
troubleshoot.fix: Classic format mismatch: PuTTY needs the key in .ppk (convert with PuTTYgen > Load > Save private key) or paste the openssh-format public key exactly as one line into authorized_keys.

costNote: Free: OpenSSH ships with Windows and Linux; PuTTY is free (MIT).

gates: Download VirtualBox 7.x for Windows hosts from virtualbox.org/wiki/Downloads plus the matching Extension Pack (needed for USB 2/3 and RDP). Install both; accept the network-interface warnings during install (brief disconnect is normal).

Decide: Hyper-V OR VirtualBox as your daily hypervisor — do not run both actively (see IL27-INST-03 troubleshooting). If Hyper-V is enabled, either disable it or accept VirtualBox's slower Hyper-V-backed mode.

Create a host-only network for the lab: File > Tools > Network Manager > Create a host-only adapter (vboxnet0), set IPv4 192.168.56.1/24, enable its DHCP server (range .100-.200). This mirrors the course's lab subnet.
Create a test VM: Linux/Ubuntu 64-bit, 2 GB RAM, 20 GB VDI dynamically allocated, attach the Ubuntu Server ISO (IL27-INST-08), NIC 1 = NAT (internet), NIC 2 = Host-only (lab). Boot and install.
Install Guest Additions after the OS is up (Devices > Insert Guest Additions CD image, then run it) for smooth mouse, shared clipboard, and proper resolution.

checkpoints.expected: 7.x.x version string
vboxnet0 with IP 192.168.56.1 listed
Your test VM listed while running

troubleshoot.issue: VM fails to start: 'VT-x is not available'
troubleshoot.fix: Enable VT-x/AMD-V in firmware AND resolve the Hyper-V conflict — bcdedit /set hypervisorlaunchtype off + reboot if you chose VirtualBox as primary.

troubleshoot.issue: Host-only adapter missing after install
troubleshoot.fix: Recreate it in Network Manager; on some Windows builds you must run VirtualBox elevated once to register the adapter.

troubleshoot.issue: Guest Additions ISO will not mount
troubleshoot.fix: Eject any mounted ISO first (Devices > Optical Drives > Remove disk), then re-insert the Guest Additions image.

costNote: Free: VirtualBox base package is GPL; the Extension Pack is free for personal/educational use.
